plan.description: Check actual pipelineDecode calls against the AppendFuture.Response access precondition using completed instrumented futures with nil and non-nil errors.

harness.description: The supplied Consumer interface permits delivery of a chosen completed future, and instrumented future methods expose actual decoder invocations. An unbuffered channel handoff establishes that the decoder selected the future before the harness closes its stop channel. The selected case runs before the decoder can select shutdown again; finishCh establishes completion before final fixture fields are read. This requires no sleeps, lock bypasses, or assumed transport ordering. Both cases use equal request and response terms and empty entries. The nil-error case supplies Success=true and exercises the permitted response path through notifyAll; the non-nil-error case supplies Success=false. The oracle measures whether Error returned nil before Response access.
semantic_changes: Substitute an instrumented AppendPipeline and already completed AppendFuture for network submission and decoding. Actual Raft.pipelineDecode and its reached helpers remain unchanged.

Record method invocations and error status in the future implementation. Response returns fixture storage even when called without validation so the actual caller can finish and the access violation can be measured.

Use empty-entry requests, equal terms, an initialized zero-value followerReplication with nextIndex=1, and an empty notification map. This avoids invoking commitment.match and the higher-term logging branch.
Stop through the existing stop channel after actual future handoff, independently of whether Error or Response is invoked. Read final fields only after finishCh closes.

legality.derivation: AppendPipeline.Consumer delivers ready futures; its contract does not guarantee nil errors. The network producer explicitly completes a future with the decoding error and then delivers it. The substituted future supplies a completed, stable error result and correlated request and response storage. Empty requests are handled by updateLastAppended without dereferencing commitment, and notifyAll accepts an empty map. The supplied helper bodies require no additional fixture dependencies for these paths. The Response-access requirement comes from the interface documentation, independently of pipelineDecode's implementation.
legality.applicability: Legal local interface inputs for the selected caller-contract check. The controlled non-nil error does not assert any particular real failed-response contents or execution of a network producer.
unresolved: The substituted producer does not establish built-in transport reproduction or a legal end-to-end replication history.
Concrete appendFuture accessor behavior remains outside this substituted-interface experiment.
alternatives: Consumer delivery can establish completed decoding without establishing a nil error.
Success=false can prevent endpoint reporting while leaving the Response access precondition independently violated.

grounding.derivation: AppendFuture.Response requires Error to have returned and limits validity to success. Each response_access event is emitted by the instrumented method upon an actual call from pipelineDecode. Its assertion field reflects whether a preceding Error invocation on that same future returned nil. The decoder calls methods synchronously, so entry into Response follows the preceding Error return when such a call occurred. Neither the input error nor the measured validation field filters result events.
grounding.applicability: Every actual Response invocation on either delivered fixture future, correlated with the prior input_ready event by its independent operation_id.
unresolved: A measured access discrepancy alone does not establish an unsupported endpoint or a consensus consequence.
alternatives: A consumer may reject an error future without calling Response; that path produces no Response-access violation and requires completed processing evidence before a bounded hold interpretation.

observable_properties.description: Every observed Response access must follow a completed Error call returning nil on the same future. Error status and method ordering are observed independently of response fields. Missing delivery, processing, or decoder completion leaves a bounded absence claim unresolved.

uncertainties: The experiment substitutes the completion producer and checks the actual consumer only; it does not execute the network pipeline.
The non-nil-error response has Success=false. No coexistence of a real error and Success=true is assumed or established.
Empty requests exercise successful response interpretation and notification without establishing any voter endpoint, published commitment, or application effect.

Method-access measurements require operation-correlated input events. Bounded absence additionally requires future delivery, observed processing, and decoder_completed; timeout or missing events remain unknown.
The local interface result does not resolve peer replacement, replication-context ownership, or end-to-end reachability.

partial_design: The requested helper bodies support the existing fixture: setLastContact updates its protected timestamp, and notifyAll safely handles an empty map. The completed design retains the selected obligation and invocation-order oracle, calls actual pipelineDecode, and ends independently through its existing stop channel after future handoff.
